correctness.rationale: The update on any labelled K_{m,n} is an exact lift of one of 729 truncated count signatures supplemented by six origin-colour tags; truncation at two preserves each successor-contact threshold. For every signature the supplied explicit checker verifies the tagged state at times 3 and 15 agrees, and the exact least-period table is 666/15/48 for periods 1/3/4. Origin tags recover all labelled vertex states even when population counts repeat early. The 15 period-three signatures and the 48 fully listed period-four types give the exact binomial basin formulas. Independent direct vertex evolution enumerated 164,754 initial configurations on six graphs, verifying counts and sharp witness. A separate exact integer combinatorial check verified expressions through size 100. Binomial expansion proves asymptotic coefficients. These finite checks prove all sizes only by the stated exact finite-quotient reduction; testing a finite number of unbounded graph sizes alone would not prove the theorem.

value.rationale: Threshold-two CCA on a complete bipartite contact network is a natural finite synchronization/oscillation model. The all-size exact basin census distinguishes periodic populations from trajectories attracted to them and the full labelled period from count-period aliasing. The absence of three-cycles for intermediate community sizes 4 and 5 despite their reappearance at 6+ is a reentrant structural threshold that cannot be inferred from the general period restriction. The exponential period-four tail and fixed-point tail give quantitatively distinct rare-event scales. A universal 729-state origin-tag quotient is a useful reusable proof method for threshold-count dynamics.
